report.summary: The served source covers the existing label and markup grammars plus a static-relation form, but it does not contain the smaller shared descriptor that the fixture describes. First, no native form-source parser exists: assessmentEvidenceScope can admit only 'The static … control markup in <one file> must use input type …', and every other fixture source string is routed to unclassified requirements or to the observation pool from lines 172-180 of lib/assessment-evidence-scope.ts. Second, the shared parse is declared in each parser separately: source-literal-directive.ts and static-markup-directive each own their own grammar. The only shared quotation check in the packet, the label witness, parses with parse5 and lists the missing labels, which the server turns into insufficient_evidence, never into a supported verdict. So the C34 failure (ordinary rows demanded as one exact sentence, ordinary template-email labels falsely supported) is still the observed behaviour, not a closed planning problem. Planning gaps found: (a) the label grammar's LABEL token allows no colon, digit-leading, ampersand, or non-ASCII characters; (b) the intended radio grammar in staticRelationDirective would not parse the fixture's native radio rows; (c) the form context in labelsIn can be satisfied by form-associated labels that are outside the real form; (d) the no-exact-sentence guard has no closed grammar and overlaps the existing title-comma special case; (e) with the proposed owners, the wrong-value fixture could receive a supported verdict from the existing positive-literal promotion; (f) the 'template-email label falsely supported' family is not yet closed by the label witness alone. No universal grammar and no accuracy claim is made.

findings.title: Label grammar rejects colon-, digit-, ampersand-, and non-ASCII label texts that the native fixtures use
findings.evidence: LABEL = /^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9 *'’()_-]{0,79}$/u (line 7) is applied to each value split by parseSourceLiteralDirective (lines 33-35). The first character must be A-Z, the remaining characters come from an ASCII set, and ':' is not in that set. Fixture files (tests/fixtures/three-gaps-cycle35-plan-context.json) use label texts 'Customer name:', 'Telephone:', 'E-mail address:' (line 320), and the radio/checkbox option texts 'Small', 'Extra Cheese' (lines 495, 346). A directive of the form 'X form source content must include the labels "Name:" and "E-mail:" …' is a candidate, because isSourceLiteralDirectiveCandidate (line 14) accepts 'prefix + include the labels', and parseSourceLiteralDirective returns undefined. assessmentEvidenceScope (lib/assessment-evidence-scope.ts, line 171) then classifies the criterion as requires_observation/unclassified_requirement and forces insufficient_evidence.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (not executed): call parseSourceLiteralDirective('Contact form source content must include the labels "Name:" and "Telephone:".'). PREFIX (line 4) matches 'Contact form source content must '. /^(label|include the labels|…)/ then matches, giving values ['Name:','Telephone:']. LABEL.test('Name:') is false, so the function returns undefined at line 35. Separately, any value beginning with a digit or '&' also fails the ^[A-Z] anchor even when it is valid native text such as '11:00'.
findings.suggestion: Keep the quotation and list grammar as it is, but add a closed alternative that accepts at most six complete quoted tokens ("…" or '…'), each 1-120 characters long with no control characters or line breaks, alongside the legacy LABEL token. The action-verb and 'and/or' rejections still apply. The same parse must feed both admission and the citation witness, so a label containing ':' is never silently downgraded.

findings.title: Existing type grammar binds an element keyword instead of the named input, and the generic literalList drops the 'and' separator in radio lists
findings.evidence: Pattern line 43 /^(CONTEXT) source (?:email|password|text|tel|number|url|search) input must have type=(…)\.$/ captures only the file context. The fixture source 'The static source in forms-post.html must declare custtel as a tel input and custemail as an email input.' does not match it, and isStaticMarkupDirectiveCandidate (line 68) does not cover 'custtel as a …'. It also does not match the proposed staticRelationDirective. The scope therefore falls to unclassified (lib/assessment-evidence-scope.ts, line 171), and the native name→type fact can never be witnessed. In addition, literalList (lines 17-31) does not keep the separator: on ',\s*(?:and\s+)?|\s+and\s+' it advances by separator length minus one, so the next value starts at the 'a' of 'and'. relationLabels (lib/assessment-evidence-scope.ts, line 102) is left with the same risk if it takes the same approach for three or more labels.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (not executed): with value 'Small and Medium and Large', the first separator ' and ' matches at i=5, so start becomes 11, which points at 'and Large'. The resulting value is 'and Large', which continuation.test (line 14) rejects because of 'and'. The list is therefore rejected, or mis-split if the word passes. For the tel/email directive, no route exists from criterion source to a descriptor, so the C34 'ordinary row' insufficient_evidence result is unchanged for native input types.
findings.suggestion: Add an atomic-family pattern that binds '<name> as a <type> input' to staticRelationDirective, for example 'The static source in FILE must declare NAME as a TYPE input', repeated with 'and' for a second name, using INPUT_TYPES. Fix the separator arithmetic (set start to the end of the separator, for example start = i + separator[0].length) in one shared list splitter used by both parsers. Add one literal witness per name and type that requires the same <input name=NAME … type=TYPE> start tag, and otherwise treat TYPE as unsupported, never as automatic.

findings.title: Intended radio/checkbox grammar does not parse the fixture's quoted native radio rows or the checkbox wording
findings.evidence: The radio or-group regex (line 137) requires '^The (\S+) source content must pair (.+) radio labels with values (.+) under the same NAME name$'. Its label list and value list share relationLabels (line 102), which accepts no quotation marks and requires A-Z initial capitals. The values split at line 141 on whitespace, and line 142 requires values of the form 0 or [1-9]\d{0,2}. The fixture source (line 495), 'The source content in forms-post.html must pair Small and Medium and Large radio labels …', therefore binds the file to the bare word 'source', which is not an .html path. The checkbox family (line 682) '… must associate Bacon … checkbox labels with …' has no pattern at all. Neither parse, and both fall to unclassified.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (not executed): relationFile('source') runs assertStaticPath('source') and then checks the .html extension, so it returns undefined. staticRelationDirective therefore returns undefined at line 140. The criterion is then admitted only as an observation requirement, and the wrong-value mutation at fixture line 695 (value="medium" on the Large radio) cannot produce a deterministic changes_suggested from the descriptor itself.
findings.suggestion: Give the grammar one explicit file form and up to six quoted or plain-token labels paired with same-cardinality literal names. Accept each label paired with its value on a same-name radio/checkbox group. Do not accept values outside the declared group name, or controls outside the required form. Do not reuse relationLabels for a different syntax.

findings.title: The 'form' context is satisfied by form-associated labels that are outside the real form
findings.evidence: Line 28 sets group to the start offset of the enclosing <form>, and labels nested in a form inherit that group. The parser has no handling for a label with a form="id" attribute. A <label form="f" for="mail">E-mail:</label> that sits outside <form id="f"> and inside a template is skipped, but the same label sitting outside the form as ordinary markup keeps its text and can, together with the in-form labels, form one complete group. Rule 50 of the plan requires the witness to be tied to the same actual form and group.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (not executed): given <form id="f"><label>Name:</label>…</form><label form="f" for="mail">E-mail:</label>, labelsIn produces Name: with group formOffset and E-mail: with form undefined, because it is not a descendant of <form>. The form-context filter at line 67 drops the E-mail: label and reports incomplete. Given a mutation that places the out-of-form label inside a template, it is skipped, which is correct. The bug is the loose mapping of 'form' to source nesting only, not to actual association. If a future native descriptor reuses this grouping for pair checks, it would mis-group and needs form association semantics.
findings.suggestion: When the descriptor requires the same actual form, group labels by the nearest form owner, which is the associated <form> when form="id" is set, otherwise the nearest ancestor form. Exclude any label whose form owner is not the required form, and treat an unresolvable owner as unknown.

findings.title: Promotion of a bare supported verdict to the positive-literal explanation short-circuits mixed or wrong-value owner evidence
findings.evidence: At lines 350-357, when the business check is dynamic_or_unsupported and positiveLiteralCheck returns covered, the explanation is replaced and the status stays supported. If the native witness is wired into the same node, a criterion with several atomic facts (radio pairs or named types) can receive a supported verdict from one covered positive literal while another fact is wrong. The wrong-value fixture (line 695) expects changes_suggested but published insufficient_evidence (line 748). In addition, the existing grammar fix would supply a descriptor for the wrong-owner case, and the first positive literal could take over the explanation.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (not executed): raw supported with citations covering only the Small and Medium owners, while the Large radio has value="medium". positiveLiteralCheck(criterion, checkedCitations) returns covered for the single literal it recognises, and lines 353-357 set the explanation and leave status supported. No per-fact counter-example check runs before the promotion.
findings.suggestion: Require every atomic fact in the descriptor (each label/name/value/type/attribute tuple) to be witnessed before the positive-literal promotion replaces the explanation. Any witnessed contradiction (a same-name or same-file owner with a different value or type) must set changes_suggested. Otherwise downgrade to insufficient_evidence or keep the raw supported verdict without any promotion.

findings.title: Existing label witness, as wired, only downgrades and has no closed path for the template-email false support or the required ordinary-row derivation
findings.evidence: Line 20 imports createAssessmentLabelCitationCheck, and line 406-411 turns incomplete or unknown into insufficient_evidence. Nothing in the served logic prevents a model from returning supported on a decoy (template or script label text) when the citations cover the real non-inert labels plus enough unrelated span to satisfy the group. The ordinary-row case (fixture line 26, 'Earth is Our world' as a row header plus cell) has no descriptor that covers the ASSESSMENT_FACT_RELATION_GUIDANCE sentence structure, and lines 312-324 only convert a changes_suggested verdict on missing exact text to insufficient_evidence when business checks are unknown. A raw supported verdict for that row is never checked against owner relationships.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (not executed): for coverage-2 in the first knownFailure, the raw changes_suggested comes from the business check being unknown, and it is downgraded at lines 312-324. Nothing in the cited label witness, presence check or list check examines the row-th and td relationship, so a model returning supported for the same row would be published as supported. For the template-email case, the witness at lines 66-79 ignores template descendants, so a citation covering the real Name: and Message: labels plus a span containing template text is still judged incomplete (safe downgrade). Safe, but the plan gap is the missing one-shared-descriptor wiring, not an executed proof.
findings.suggestion: Wire the one shared parse so that admission and witness both consume the same descriptor. For the label family, require every listed label's complete owner to be a non-inert, same-page or same-form label. Treat any citation that covers only inert or decoy text as not witnessed, and never promote to supported from it. For the ordinary row family, add a closed 'header plus bound cell' descriptor with exact owner checks before any status other than insufficient_evidence can be published.

limitations: Read-only, source-packet-only review. No files changed; no shell, test, typecheck, browser or runtime checks performed. All reproductions are labelled reasoning traces.

Runtime facts are not verified: the served source contains no native form-source parser, no ordinary-row descriptor and no nonexact-negative guard. plans such as parseNativeFormSourceDirective and createNativeFormCitationCheck appear only in the fixture plannedInterfaces (tests/fixtures/three-gaps-cycle35-plan-context.json, lines 872-876), so they cannot be reviewed as code.
parse5 node shapes (for example, DefaultTreeAdapterTypes) are used as they are written in the source. I did not verify its node or sourceCodeLocation semantics at runtime.
The MDN August corpus, the official rule text and the AgentReceipt references were not supplied. Their claims were neither inspected nor confirmed.
The fixture is treated as untrusted data. Its publishedItems and reference expectations describe observed or intended behaviour only, not verified outcomes.
